title: Muhammara
description: Roasted red peppers and walnuts pounded into a coarse, brick-red dip, sharpened with pomegranate molasses and Aleppo pepper. Nothing is cooked — it is fifteen minutes and a food processor, and it is better made an hour ahead.
notes: Jarred peppers are what make this a no-cook dish. If you would rather roast your own, blacken and peel three large red peppers first and let them drain properly — the texture is better and the timing is no longer fifteen minutes.

steps.text: Drain the roasted red peppers and pat them dry between two tea towels until they stop leaving damp marks.
steps.tip: Wet peppers are the single reason muhammara turns into a puddle in the bowl. Take this further than feels necessary.

steps.text: Pulse the walnuts and breadcrumbs together until they look like coarse wet sand.
steps.tip: Stop while you can still see individual pieces. Once it goes to paste the dip loses its grain and reads as hummus.

steps.text: Add the peppers, garlic, cumin, Aleppo pepper, salt, pomegranate molasses and lemon juice, and pulse in short bursts until it comes together but stays rough.
With the motor running slowly, pour in the olive oil until the mixture turns glossy and holds a spoon mark.
Taste and push it one way or the other — more molasses for sweetness, more lemon for edge, more Aleppo for heat. Spread it into a shallow bowl and leave it to settle.
steps.tip: Straight out of the processor it tastes disjointed. An hour on the counter is what pulls it into one thing.
